User Actions#

User actions routes module.

This module handles event viewing, searching/filtering, booking, cancellation, and password management for authenticated users.

events_js()[source]#

Load the events javascript.

Returns:

The javascript ‘events.js’ file.

Return type:

Any

_get_booked_counts(db, event_ids)[source]#

Return {event_id: confirmed_booking_count} for the given event ids.

A single grouped query instead of one COUNT(*) per event, so this stays flat regardless of how many events are being displayed.

_local_day_bounds_utc(date_str, tz)[source]#

Convert a local YYYY-MM-DD string to naive UTC [start, end) bounds.

Raises:

ValueError – If date_str isn’t a valid YYYY-MM-DD date.

_parse_event_query_params(args)[source]#

Parse and lightly validate the /events (and /api/v1/events) query params.

_apply_date_range(query, filters, tz)[source]#

Apply an optional ?from=&to= range filter, clamped to MAX_DATE_RANGE_DAYS.

Returns:

The filtered query, and whether the requested

range had to be clamped.

Return type:

Tuple[Query, bool]

_apply_sort(query, sort)[source]#

Order the event query per the resolved sort filter value.

_load_events(db, user_id, tz, now_utc, filters)[source]#

Query and annotate events matching filters for the given user.

Applies the search/date/sort filters in SQL, then attaches the per-event is_fully_booked/is_user_booked flags (one grouped booking count query, not one per event), and finally applies the avail_only filter in Python against that small, already-bounded result set.

Returns:

The matching events, and whether an

explicit ?from=&to= range had to be clamped.

Return type:

Tuple[List[Event], bool]

_serialize_event(event)[source]#

Serialize an annotated Event row for the JSON API.

get_month_day_set(db, year, month, tz)[source]#

Return the set of local ISO date strings with >=1 event in the given month.

At most ~31 rows thanks to AdminService’s “one event per day” rule, so this is always a cheap query regardless of how large the events table is. (Mirrors admin_dashboard.get_month_events’s shape - both are thin wrappers around the shared month_utc_bounds helper, returning different projections of the same month-scoped query.)

build_calendar_weeks(year, month, day_set, today_str)[source]#

Build a Sunday-first month grid for the date-picker.

Returns:

Weeks, each a list of 7 day-cell dicts (leading/

trailing days from adjacent months are included to fill the grid).

Return type:

List[List[dict]]

_build_event_view_context(db, user_id)[source]#

Load everything the events page (and its API counterpart) need.

Shared by the Jinja route (first paint) and the JSON API route (re-fetches on filter/date/sort change), so both stay in sync against one query implementation.

events()[source]#

Render the event booking page: search, date/date-range filters, sorting, and a “browse by month” date-picker.

Booking and cancellation are handled by the dedicated /booking and /cancel_booking/<event_id> routes, not by this view.

api_events()[source]#

JSON API: list events matching the same filters as the /events page.

booking()[source]#

Handle event booking requests.

Prevents booking if the event has already started or finished.

cancel_booking(event_id)[source]#

Cancel a booking for a specific event.

Prevents cancellation if the event has already started or finished.

change_password_js()[source]#

Load the change password javascript.

Returns:

The javascript ‘change_password.js’ file.

Return type:

Any

change_password()[source]#

Handle password change requests securely.

Ensures that the old password is correct, validates the new password, and updates the user’s password if everything is correct.
